key_insight: MLExpert turns long-horizon machine learning engineering into an agentic optimization problem, using outcome-guided supervision and windowed reinforcement learning to improve autonomous experiment planning and adaptation.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a practical recipe for building AI agents that can manage iterative ML workflows, making it relevant for automated model tuning, benchmark optimization, and broader AI-for-AI engineering pipelines.
method: Built Kaggle-MLE Factory to generate executable MLE tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation.
Used hierarchical agentic SFT to transfer general tool-use and coding skills into machine learning engineering behavior.
Introduced Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) with shared rewards over multi-turn execution windows and asynchronous policy correction.
evidence_signal: On MLE-Bench Lite, the average medal rate improved from 37.9% to 72.7%, and the model performed comparably to larger frontier systems such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3.
watch_item: The approach depends on costly long-run experiment trajectories and carefully designed execution windows, so stability and sample efficiency may be sensitive to task complexity and feedback noise.
paper_title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
